key_insight: Adding ADR-based physical knowledge to TSMixer offered limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with a purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, added hybrid-model complexity may not deliver reliable gains in accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries; hybrids appeared to converge slightly faster but showed no consistent improvements in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or forecasting settings.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
